Committee: Governmental Affairs
Sponsor: Orr
Analyst: John Friedenreich
Date: 02/09/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 112 as introduced would reduce the additional license tax and registration fee of $200, previously established for battery electric vehicles pursuant to the Rebuild Alabama Act, to $50 for electric low speed vehicles (LSV) that are registered and operated on the public (non-interstate) highways of this state.  Based on the number of LSV's registered in FY 2020, beginning January 1, 2022 this could reduce collections from LSV's by an estimated $40,200 per year, as follows:
Public Road and Bridge Fund
$20,000
Counties and Municipalities
$10,000
Rebuild Alabama Fund
$10,000
Jimmy Holley, Chairperson
Governmental Affairs

Committee: Ways and Means General Fund
Sponsor: Orr
Analyst: John Friedenreich
Date: 02/22/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 112 as passed the Senate would reduce the current additional license tax and registration fee of either $200 or $100, established for battery or plug-in hybrid electric vehicles, respectively, pursuant to the Rebuild Alabama Act, to $50 for electric low speed vehicles (LSV) that are registered and operated on the public (non-interstate) highways of this state. Based on the number of LSV's registered in fiscal year 2020, beginning January 1, 2022, this bill would reduce LSV license tax and registration fee receipts to the following funds by the following estimated amounts:
Public Road and Bridge Fund
$20,000
Counties and Municipalities
$10,000
Rebuild Alabama Fund
$10,000
Total
$40,000
Steve Clouse, Chair
Ways and Means General Fund

Committee: Ways and Means General Fund
Sponsor: Orr
Analyst: John Friedenreich
Date: 02/24/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 112 as substituted and reported by the Committee on Ways and Means General Fund would reduce the current additional license tax and registration fee of either $200 or $100, established for battery or plug-in hybrid electric vehicles, respectively, pursuant to the Rebuild Alabama Act, to $50 for electric low speed vehicles (LSV) that are registered and operated on the public (non-interstate) highways of this state. Based on the number of LSV's registered in fiscal year 2020, beginning January 1, 2022, this bill would reduce LSV license tax and registration fee receipts to the following funds by the following estimated amounts:
Public Road and Bridge Fund
$20,000
Counties and Municipalities
$10,000
Rebuild Alabama Fund
$10,000
Total
$40,000
Additionally, this bill establishes that the Alabama Department of Revenue is responsible for the distribution of the additional annual license and registration fees for electric vehicles beginning October 1, 2021, which will increase the administrative obligations of the department by an undetermined amount.
Kyle South, Vice Chair
Ways and Means General Fund

Committee: Ways and Means General Fund
Sponsor: Singleton
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 04/12/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 345 as passed the Senate reestablishes the Prison PREP Pilot Program for Small Business Development for Ex-Offenders, previously under the Department of Corrections (DOC), that expired on December 31, 2020, under the Board of Pardons and Paroles and the DOC effective July 1, 2021 through December 31, 2026, subject to the availability of funds. This would increase the obligations of the Board of Pardons and Paroles, by an undetermined amount to: 1) establish training locations and funding for participants to receive training on establishment of small businesses; 2) provide assistance in obtaining small business funding; 3) partner with entities to provide mentorship to individuals for three years; and 4) to provide an annual report on the effectiveness of the program to the Legislature and the Legislative Services Agency by the fifth legislative day of each regular session.
For fiscal years 2019, 2020, and 2021, DOC was appropriated $100,000 from the State General Fund for the program that expired on December 31, 2020. The House Passed General Fund Budget for fiscal year 2022 currently appropriates $100,000 from the State General Fund to DOC for this program.
This bill could further increase the obligations of J. F. Ingram State Community College, paid from the Education Trust Fund, by an undetermined amount, to provide training in small business development to inmates exiting the correctional system.
Steve Clouse, Chair
Ways and Means General Fund

Committee: Finance and Taxation General Fund
Sponsor: Singleton
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 03/31/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 345 as introduced, reestablishes the Prison PREP Pilot Program for Small Business Development for Ex-Offenders, previously under the Department of Corrections, that expired on December 31, 2020, under the Board of Pardons and Paroles and the Department of Corrections effective July 1, 2021 through December 31, 2026. This would increase the obligations of the Board of Pardons and Paroles, by an undetermined amount to: 1) establish training locations and funding for individuals to receive training; 2) partner with entities to provide mentorship to individuals for three years; and 3) to provide an annual report on the effectiveness of the program to the Legislature and the Legislative Services Agency by the fifth legislative day of each regular session.
For fiscal years 2019, 2020, and 2021, the Department of Corrections was appropriated $100,000 from the State General Fund for the program that expired on December 31, 2020. The House Passed General Fund Budget for fiscal year 2022 currently appropriates from the State General Fund $100,000.
This bill could further increase the obligations of J. F. Ingram State Community College, paid from the Education Trust Fund, by an undetermined amount, to provide training in small business development to currently incarcerated inmates and those inmates that have been released.
Greg Albritton, Chairperson
Finance and Taxation General Fund
